claim: Headscale v0.29.7 linux_arm64, Tailscale v1.104.6 arm64 tgz, nats-server v2.15.2 and natscli v0.5.1 downloads matched both the pinned sha256 and the upstream checksum files; Go 1.27.4 matched the go.dev hash; derper was built from tailscale.com@v1.104.6 with module checksums verified (built binary sha256 12ab8be0740e98645412926e33fe521a605af4f63f84054c586680dbbfc28fca)

A self-hosted Headscale v0.29.7 enrolled three nodes (hub and two homes behind separate NATs) with single-use tagged pre-auth keys (1 h, not reusable); a fourth tailscaled given an already-used key was refused with 'backend error: authkey already used'

Two Tailscale v1.104.6 nodes each behind a Linux nftables masquerade NAT that drops every new inbound connection established a direct WireGuard path (UDP 41641 between the two NAT public addresses, ~48 ms median with 40 ms of netem RTT); no port forward or inbound accept existed, TCP 1-1024/41641 and UDP 41641/3478 probes from outside got no answer, and every conntrack flow of the home nodes was originated inside

With all UDP from one home LAN dropped at its NAT, Tailscale v1.104.6 fell back to the self-hosted DERP relay (derper from tailscale.com@v1.104.6, TCP 443) within 10 s; 20/20 pings went via DERP(onemind-hub) at 139 ms median vs 48 ms direct, the allowed service and the NATS leaf TLS handshake kept working, and the path returned to direct on the first ping after the block was removed

Exploratory: with one NAT switched to endpoint-dependent mapping (nftables 'masquerade random') the two homes did not get a direct path within 40 pings and stayed on the self-hosted DERP relay (~130 ms); traffic kept working

NATS leaves (nats-server v2.15.2, JetStream domains node-home-a/node-home-b, stream ONEMIND_NODE_OUTBOX) connected to the hub's leaf port over the WireGuard mesh with TLS and per-node passwords buffered 500 events each during a 30-minute total hub-link outage (every publish acked locally); 44 s after the link returned the hub stream NODE_EVENTS held exactly 1200 messages with each node's sequence 1..600 in order, no gaps, no duplicates

With nats-server v2.15.2 default ping settings and a link that drops silently (no TCP reset), a leaf detected the loss after 194 s ('Slow Consumer (Write Deadline)') and the hub marked both leaves stale after 405 s; after the link returned both leaves reconnected within 4-8 s

A nats-server v2.15.2 leaf listener with a tls block and per-user leafnode authorization refused a plaintext CONNECT ('TLS Handshake Failure'), a leaf that did not trust the box CA (x509 'certificate signed by unknown authority') and a leaf with a wrong password ('authentication error'); bound to the hub's mesh address it was not reachable on the hub's public address

A nats-server v2.15.2 leaf remote with no tls block upgrades to TLS on its own when the hub's INFO says tls_required, and verifies the hub with the process trust store (it connected when SSL_CERT_FILE held the box CA, and failed x509 verification without it)

A Headscale v0.29.7 policy generated from OneMind roles enforced per-port rules on Tailscale v1.104.6: in 3/3 attempts home A reached tag:leaf:9001 on home B and received no bytes from home B:9002 or hub:9002, while both 9002 services answered locally

On a 4 vCPU / 4 GiB arm64 VM (Apple M5 Max host), idle tailscaled v1.104.6 plus a NATS v2.15.2 leaf with JetStream used 56.4 MiB PSS combined on average (60.3 MiB max; tailscaled 29.1, leaf 27.3) and 0.42 % of one vCPU over 600 s; CPU is a lower bound for a Pi 5

nats-server v2.15.2 rejects a 'permissions' field on a user in leafnodes.authorization.users ('unknown field "permissions"'); the config reload failed and the old config stayed active, and a leaf could publish on another node's subjects (3/3 reached a hub subscriber). Per-node subject isolation on leaf links therefore needs accounts or operator/JWT mode, not config users
derper (tailscale.com@v1.104.6) ran with -verify-clients against the hub's own tailscaled and relayed traffic for enrolled nodes; refusal of an unenrolled client was not tested
